title: AI cyber power is now handed out in tiers
content: On 6 October 2026 Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program into three access tiers that decide how much offensive-security help Claude will give a verified organisation.

title: Defense, Red Team and Specialized
content: The three tiers are Defense Access, Red Team Access and Specialized Access. Each adds permissions on top of the last.

title: The public model still refuses
content: In Anthropic's own tests, the generally available Claude Opus 5.5 blocked every one of the cyber tasks on the first prompt.

title: Verified red teams get the full capability
content: Under Red Team Access the model blocked nothing and completed 34 of 50 test tasks, which Anthropic says matches unrestricted performance.

title: Glasswing folds into the programme
content: Members of Project Glasswing, Anthropic's earlier Mythos security partnership, move automatically into the new Specialized Access tier without reapplying.

title: The same week, AI-linked hacks hit Korean banks
content: Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and Hana Bank all disclosed customer data leaks around 2 October 2026, with analysts pointing to AI tooling in at least one attack.

title: Seoul ordered emergency checks
content: South Korea's Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting and ordered checks of externally accessible banking systems.

title: Wall Street is worried too
content: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon told Bloomberg Television that "risks from AI went up 10-fold after Mythos", according to Fox News' live coverage on 6 October.

title: The labs won't promise perfect safety
content: At a New York City Council hearing on 6 October, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google representatives declined to guarantee their systems will always follow safeguards.

title: The story in one line
content: Frontier labs are rationing AI hacking ability by identity and purpose, just as evidence grows that attackers already have capable AI tools of their own.

title: Defense Access: the entry tier
content: Defense Access covers defensive work: security operations centres, incident response, malware reverse-engineering and vulnerability analysis.

title: Who can get Defense Access
content: Corporate security teams, nonprofits, universities, government bodies, critical infrastructure operators, smaller security firms, open-source maintainers and individual researchers with a disclosure record.

title: Defense Access is fast
content: Anthropic says it aims to review Defense Access applications in a few days.

title: Red Team Access: authorised attacks
content: Red Team Access adds authorised penetration testing and red-teaming on top of everything in Defense Access.

title: Who can get Red Team Access
content: In-house red teams, government red teams and professional security or penetration-testing firms. Individual researchers are not eligible.

title: Red Team Access is slower
content: Applications take a few weeks to review. Organisations get Defense Access while they wait.

title: Some lines stay closed even for red teams
content: Real-time blocks still stop actions that could cause physical harm or mass disruption, such as deploying ransomware or damaging physical systems.

title: Specialized Access: safety-critical systems
content: Specialized Access permits testing systems that affect public welfare: flight operating systems, power grids, telecom networks, interbank transfer infrastructure and government administrative networks.

title: Specialized Access involves Washington
content: Anthropic says Specialized Access applications are reviewed in collaboration with the US government and are limited to verified organisations.

title: Where the programme runs
content: The programme is available on the Claude Platform, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry. On Amazon Bedrock it is limited to customers eligible for Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.

title: How Anthropic tested the tiers
content: Anthropic ran 50 trials on Claude Opus 5.5: five attempts on each of 10 challenges from its CyScenarioBench evaluation.

title: General availability: everything blocked
content: Without any verified access, the model blocked all tasks at the first prompt.

title: Defense Access: 46 of 50 blocked
content: With Defense Access, 46 of the 50 offensive trials were still blocked and four succeeded.

title: Red Team Access: zero blocks
content: With Red Team Access, no trials were blocked and 34 of 50 tasks were completed.

title: Why the tests matter
content: The results show the tiers are enforced by the model's behaviour at run time, not just by a contract or a sign-up form.

title: Defence is not a loophole
content: Four successes out of 50 under Defense Access suggests the defensive tier leaks a little offensive capability, which Anthropic chose to publish.

title: 129,000 vulnerabilities from Glasswing partners
content: Anthropic says Project Glasswing partners found 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.

title: 5,500 more in open source
content: Anthropic's own open-source scanning added 5,500 verified vulnerabilities between April and October 2026.

title: Over 33,000 critical or high
content: Of the combined total, more than 33,000 were rated critical or high severity.

title: The real count is likely higher
content: Anthropic says the true impact is likely "at least five times higher" because it only collected partial data.

title: Months or years of work, compressed
content: "Several partners told us that the models had increased their rate of vulnerability finding by months or even years," Anthropic wrote.

title: Why Mythos was held back
content: Bloomberg Law reported in July that Anthropic judged its Mythos model too good at finding software flaws to release safely to the general public.

title: Dimon's earlier warning
content: In July, Bloomberg Law reported Dimon calling broad Mythos access a "real issue" that government officials were addressing.

title: Shinhan Bank: about 25,000 customers
content: Shinhan Bank said roughly 25,000 customers' information was exposed through a mobile loan inquiry service.

title: KB Kookmin: 119 customers
content: KB Kookmin Bank said 119 customers' information was compromised through an employee mobile support system.

title: Hana Bank: 89 customers
content: Hana Bank said 89 customers' data was exposed through a sales support system, and that no financial transaction data leaked.

title: BNK: outsourced staff records
content: BNK Financial Group reported 11 records of outsourced employees leaked.

title: What leaked
content: Across the incidents, exposed data included names, resident registration numbers, addresses, phone numbers, employment details, annual income and loan limits.

title: Core banking held
content: All of the breaches went through loan inquiry or employee support systems rather than core banking platforms, the Korea Herald reported.

title: ARTEX AI on a Shinhan-linked server
content: Security analysts found traces of ARTEX AI, an AI penetration-testing tool, on a server linked to the Shinhan attack. Neither Shinhan nor regulators had officially confirmed its use.

title: Experts suspect AI agents
content: Yonhap, cited by Insurance Journal, reported experts believe attackers used sophisticated AI agents to probe for vulnerabilities.

title: A Korean warning on shared code
content: "Source codes are being shared indiscriminately and used for malicious AI hacking attempts," said Mun Chong-hyun of security firm Genians.

title: The president weighs in
content: President Lee Jae Myung said: "In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used," according to Fox News' live coverage.

title: Regulators move
content: The Financial Supervisory Service launched an emergency on-site inspection, and the FSC demanded stronger authentication, tighter access controls and faster threat sharing.

title: Europe's energy grid is exposed
content: Dutch researchers found 8,547 internet-facing solar and wind systems across 35 European countries, with about 181 sites potentially fully compromisable, Fox News reported.

title: Labs: perfection isn't possible
content: "It is not possible for me to commit or guarantee that any technology is without risk," OpenAI's Morgan Dwyer told the New York City Council.

title: Anthropic: the science is unsettled
content: "Candidly, the science of doing this is fundamentally hard and unsettled," said Anthropic's Logan Graham at the same hearing.

title: The council's reply
content: "We're just asking for accountability, transparency and safety overall," said Council Speaker Julie Menin.

title: OpenAI adds a kill switch for agents
content: OpenAI's Jason Kwon said the company added monitoring so staff can intervene immediately when models reach the internet unintentionally, and that it has already caught another incident.

title: South Korea goes sovereign
content: South Korea plans a $3.5 billion programme from March 2027 to build its own frontier AI model, Fox News reported.

title: Identity becomes the safety control
content: Instead of one model for everyone, the most capable cyber behaviour is unlocked by who you are and what you are verified to do.

title: Defenders get a head start
content: Tiered access aims to let banks, utilities and maintainers find flaws before attackers do, which is the case Glasswing's numbers are meant to support.

title: Attackers don't apply for access
content: The Korean bank incidents show attackers can use open-source or foreign AI tools that sit outside any lab's verification scheme.

title: Loan portals are the soft target
content: The Korean breaches hit peripheral systems such as loan inquiry tools, which suggests the edges of a network matter as much as its core.

title: Governments are in the loop
content: US government involvement in Specialized Access makes national security reviews part of how commercial AI is distributed.

title: Cloud partners become gatekeepers
content: Running the programme through Google, Microsoft and Amazon clouds means access rules travel with the platforms enterprises already use.

title: Disclosure is becoming the norm
content: Anthropic published test numbers that show its own tier leaking, and OpenAI disclosed new agent incidents. Public reporting is turning into an expectation.

title: Will other labs copy the tiers?
content: Watch whether OpenAI, Google and Meta adopt similar identity-based tiers for cyber capability.

title: Korea's official findings
content: Watch for regulators to confirm or rule out ARTEX AI in the Shinhan breach.

title: More bank disclosures
content: Watch whether other Korean financial firms report breaches as emergency checks continue.

title: Specialized Access approvals
content: Watch for the first named grid, telecom or interbank operators to join the Specialized tier.

title: New York's next move
content: Watch whether the New York City Council turns the hearing into AI safety rules.

title: Patch speed
content: Watch whether the flood of AI-found vulnerabilities outpaces maintainers' ability to fix them.

title: Snapshot date
content: This pack reflects sources opened on 7 October 2026. Later evidence should go in a new dated pack.
